one_liner: LuaJIT library that compiles tcpdump (pflang) filter expressions to Lua; 1.3-7.1x libpcap's BPF interpreter in its authors' benchmarks.
what_it_does: pflua compiles a pflang (tcpdump/pcap-filter) expression into a LuaJIT predicate function(P, length), where P is a uint8_t* packet pointer. The entry point is pf.compile_filter(str, opts). The default pipeline is pflua's own compiler. Option libpcap=true wraps pcap_offline_filter instead, bpf=true translates libpcap's BPF bytecode to Lua, and native=true emits x86 machine code through DynASM. It was written by Igalia for the Snabb user-space networking toolkit, which vendors it as lib/pflua. It is a Lua library with no C API, so it does not replace pcap_compile or pcap_offline_filter for C or C++ callers.
how_it_is_fast: The pure-Lua pipeline parses the expression, lowers it to a primitive AST, and optimizes it: constant and test folding, range inference on packet offsets, and hoisting of assertions. It then converts to A-normal form with common-subexpression elimination, then to SSA for control-flow optimization, and emits Lua source. The emitted code does one hoisted length check (e.g. 'if length < 34 then return false end'), where the BPF translation checks bounds before each load. It compares 16-bit fields in network byte order through ffi.cast loads. LuaJIT's tracing JIT then compiles only the branches the traffic actually takes. bpf-lua, which runs libpcap's own bytecode through the same LuaJIT path, landed within 2% of pflua on ping-flood, so most of the gain comes from LuaJIT trace compilation and inlining rather than from pflua's optimizer.
when_to_use: Filtering packets with tcpdump-syntax expressions inside a LuaJIT data plane such as Snabb, where the predicate inlines into your own packet loop.

Replacing libpcap's user-space BPF interpreter in a LuaJIT program: across the 18 filter rows of the four pflua-bench captures, pflua's median was 1.30x (wingolog-2 'net 178.79.150.0/24') to 7.1x ('portrange 0-5') libpcap's.
Homogeneous high-rate traffic that keeps one hot trace: on the ping-flood capture, 'tcp' ran at 89.9 MPPS against 37.9 for libpcap and 62.2 for the 2011 Linux BPF JIT.
As a worked example of compiling a filter DSL to Lua source (parse, optimize, ANF, SSA, residualize) and letting a tracing JIT specialise it.
when_not_to_use: C or C++ programs. There is no C API, so you would have to embed LuaJIT, and against JIT-compiled BPF pflua lost 5 of 18 rows: on the 1 GB capture, 'tcp port 5555' 23.6 vs 25.2 MPPS and 'portrange 0-6000' 22.0 vs 24.2 against linux-bpf; on wingolog-2, 'portrange 0-6000', 'host 178.79.150.233' and 'net 178.79.150.0/24'.

Mixed real-world traffic where filters match. The pflua-bench README attributes the wingolog-2 losses to LuaJIT trace state-transfer costs, and there bpf-lua also beat pflua on 'portrange 0-6000' (56.9 vs 47.5 MPPS).

When you need exact libpcap semantics. Open issues cover port/portrange edge cases (#243), negative numbers (#82), keyword elision (#157), IPv6 extension headers (#239), an internal error on 'ip dst 10' (#254) and encapsulations other than Ethernet (#21). The README itself warns of bugs and differences against libpcap.
When you need a maintained upstream: the last commit was 2017-01-30, there is no API documentation beyond pf.lua, and later fixes live only in Snabb's lib/pflua copy.
Workloads that need stable timing: issue #66 reports about 2x run-to-run variance (2014, garbage collection suspected) and is still open.

integration.dependencies: LuaJIT with FFI (bundled as the deps/luajit submodule from SnabbCo/luajit, installed as luajit-2.0.3); DynASM (luapower/dynasm, deps/dynasm) for the native=true backend; the system libpcap, loaded through ffi.load("pcap"), only for the libpcap and bpf pipelines
integration.min_toolchain: LuaJIT 2.0 with FFI (the Makefile builds the bundled copy); gcc to build the DynASM helper library
integration.platforms: x86-64 Linux is the only platform benchmarked (Debian, i7-3770); the native backend uses DynASM's x86 encoder; other architectures not documented
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it takes the same filter strings as pcap_compile, but returns a LuaJIT function rather than a bpf_program, so only LuaJIT code can call it

gotchas: Harness flaw against the main baseline: bench.lua calls libpcap (and the Linux JITs) through an FFI call per packet, after writing a pcap_pkthdr, while pflua's predicate inlines into the LuaJIT trace of the timing loop. The project's own native C driver (test-native/pf_test_native.c, gcc -O3, committed 2014-08-27) measured libpcap on the same ping-flood capture at 73.9 MPPS for 'icmp' and 110.6 MPPS for accept-all. The bench.lua CSVs of 2015-02-03 have 54.8 and 92.1. That is a cross-run comparison from different dates and harness versions, but against the native figure pflua's 'icmp' lead (89.9 MPPS) shrinks from 1.64x to 1.22x (derived from page data). Its README still says the two drivers give 'similar' results.

On ping-flood, pflua's four real filters ('ip', 'tcp', 'tcp port 5555', 'icmp') all land at 89.9-91.6 MPPS, and bpf-lua's at 88.2-90.5. The accept-all loop, which never reads packet bytes, runs at 127.9. Throughput does not move with filter complexity, so this workload mostly measures a shared per-packet cost plus call overhead, not filter code quality, and it cannot separate pflua's optimizer from bpf-lua.

The pflua-bench README prose ('180 MPPS', 'all results are faster than the accept all loop', 50 runs) does not match the committed CSVs: accept-all is the fastest column for every engine, and bench.mk sets ITERATIONS?=20. The pflua-native engine is listed in bench.mk, but no pflua-native CSV is committed for any scenario.

Snabb's vendored copy fixed a native-codegen bug ('fix typo bug in native codegen (xor/or emission)', 2020-02-07) and made register allocation architecture-independent; the upstream Igalia repo has neither fix, so use the Snabb copy if you need native=true.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick pflua when the job is runtime-compiled packet filters inside LuaJIT; ClangJIT and Proteus cover runtime specialisation of C++/CUDA/HIP code, and lua-resty-core and the LuaJIT FFI call-loop entries show cheap C calls from LuaJIT rather than a filter compiler. No sibling is a pflang implementation.
verified_claims_summary: pflua-bench's ping-flood test (961,180 ICMP packets, i7-3770, Debian, one warm-up, then 20 runs in one LuaJIT process, results committed 2015-02-03) gave a median of 89.9 MPPS for pflua on 'tcp', against 37.9 for Debian's system libpcap interpreter (optimizer on, version unstated), 62.2 for the 2011 Linux BPF JIT and 56.1 for the 2014 eBPF JIT (both built with gcc -O3 as user-space .so files). Every baseline was called per packet through LuaJIT's FFI, while pflua's Lua predicate was inlined.
status_note: Abandoned upstream since 2017-01-30 (Apache-2.0, 312 stars), with a maintained copy in Snabb's lib/pflua (fixes to 2020). Copyable for LuaJIT users, but the headline margin over libpcap is inflated by the per-packet FFI harness: the project's own C driver measured libpcap 'icmp' at 73.9 MPPS against 54.8 through bench.lua.
